newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan's most wanted kidnappers strike again.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's most wanted kidnappers strike again.

text.p: Three men who terrified Taiwan after allegedly kidnapping and killing the daughter of a popular actress have struck again, a prosecuting attorney said on Wednesday.

The trio, who top the island's most wanted list, made off with T$4 million (US$143,000) in ransom money after kidnapping a local businessman in Taipei last week, district prosecutor Shih Liang-po said.
"They abducted a victim in Taipei's Peitou area on August 8 and demanded a T$4 million ransom. They succeeded (again) this time," Shih told reporters.
The latest victim, a metal company owner, was released after his employees paid the ransom, the prosecutor said.
Shih said fingerprints found during the investigation indicated the kidnappers were the same men who snatched 17-year-old Pai Hsiao-yen, daughter of popular actress Pai Ping-ping, on April 14.
Thppers chopped off half of the teenager's left little finger and sent it to her mother, demanding a ransom of US$5 million.
Her mother later reported the case to police, and the kidnappers aborted a planned meeting to collect the ransom.
Police found Pai's body floating naked in a river on April 28. The kidnappers had strangled the teenager with two ropes, binding her hands and sinking her in the river with weights.

The crime rekindled anger over the failure of police to solve the gangland-style murder of Taoyuan county magistrate and seven others in his home last November or the murder of an opposition leader in southern Taiwan two weeks later.
More than 50,000 people marched in Taipei on May 4 to denounce Pai's gruesome murder and rising crime. They demanded Premier Lien Chan's resignation and a cabinet reshuffle. (US$1 = T$28)
